---
title: "Predictive Modeling of Claims Status"
author: 'Lily Nishizawa and Emma Nguyen'
date: today
format: html
---

### Abstract

Header and paragraph content was scraped from the raw webpages and processed into term frequencies of word tokens. For multi-class classification on a stratified 80/20 holdout split, the selected TF-IDF linear SVM achieved 81.3% accuracy across five webpage classes. For binary classification, a one hidden layer neural network yielded an estimated 83.2% accuracy in identifying relevant versus irrelevant pages.

### Preprocessing

Both models used cleaned paragraph text from labeled webpages. The text was cleaned by removing URLs, email addresses, punctuation, and digits, separating words that were joined together without spaces, converting to lowercase, and normalized white spaces. A TF-IDF vectorizer represented each page using word unigrams and bigrams with sublinear term-frequency scaling. Cleaned text was represented as TF-IDF weights over the most frequent words, excluding English stop words and words appearing in fewer than two pages. The vocabulary and weights were learned from the training pages only and then applied to the validation and test pages.

### Methods

**Binary classification:** The final prediction model for binary classification is a feed-forward neural network with one hidden layer of 64 neurons, dropout of 0.5, and a single sigmoid output giving the probability that a page is irrelevant. The labeled data were split into 80% training and 20% validation, stratified by class. The hyper-parameters (hidden units, dropout rate, learning rate, and number of epochs) were chosen by doing a grid search over 24 different combinations, selecting the one with the highest validation AUC. The final model with the best parameters was trained with the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.001 on binary cross-entropy loss for 10 epochs with a batch size of 32. Pages with a predicted probability above 0.5 were labeled irrelevant.

**Multi-class classification:** We compared logistic regression, a linear support vector classifier (SVM), and multinomial Naive Bayes using the same TF-IDF features. On a stratified 80/20 split (1,712 training pages and 428 validation pages; random seed 42), their validation accuracies were 78.5%, 81.3%, and 71.3%, respectively. We selected the linear SVM with class-balanced weights; the vectorizer used a minimum document frequency of one, and the SVM used its default regularization setting. The final model was then fit on all labeled pages.

### Results

**Binary classification:** The selected neural network correctly classified 328 of 394 validation pages, having a 83.2% accuracy (AUC 0.92). The table below reports sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy with each class treated as positive. Sensitivity was higher for "Relevant claim content" than for "N/A: No relevant content", indicating the model more reliably identified relevant pages. The most errors were irrelevant pages labeled as relevant (40/179).

| Class | Number of Validation pages | Sensitivity | Specificity | Accuracy |
|:--------------|--------------:|--------------:|--------------:|--------------:|
| Relevant claim content | 215 | 87.9% | 77.7% | 83.2% |
| N/A: No relevant content | 179 | 77.7% | 87.9% | 83.2% |

: With only two classes, one class's sensitivity is the specificity for the other and accuracy is the same for both. Overall, the model identified relevant pages more reliably than irrelevant ones, with the most errors being where irrelevant pages were labeled as relevant.

**Multi-class classification:** The selected SVM correctly classified 348 of 428 validation pages (81.3% accuracy; macro-F1 73.8%). The class-specific measures below treat each label as positive and all other labels as negative.

| Class | Validation pages | Sensitivity | Specificity | One-vs-rest accuracy |
|:--------------|--------------:|--------------:|--------------:|--------------:|
| N/A: No relevant content. | 203 | 82.3% | 82.7% | 82.5% |
| Other claim content | 20 | 40.0% | 97.3% | 94.6% |
| Physical Activity | 47 | 59.6% | 97.6% | 93.5% |
| Possible Fatality | 88 | 90.9% | 95.9% | 94.9% |
| Potentially unlawful activity | 70 | 92.9% | 98.0% | 97.2% |

Overall multi-class accuracy is the proportion of pages assigned the correct one of five labels. One-vs-rest accuracy is calculated separately for each class and is distinct from overall multi-class accuracy. “Other claim content” had only 20 validation examples and the lowest sensitivity (40.0%).
